summary: Core dynamically discovers a fixed native pool CPU baseline and preserves explicit feature policies per VM; no OS-specific requirements or hardcoded CPU model catalogue. API impact: changed contract, with new authenticated Core peer routes.

guide.reason: Creation defaults to the reported fixed baseline; manual models and existing saved definitions remain available, with explicit unavailable-state handling.

api.reason: Add optional VMCPU.features, Inventory.cpu_baseline, vm-cpu-baseline-v1 and authenticated Core peer capabilities/compare/baseline operations. Controller relays definitions; Core computes and validates them.

roadmap.reason: No published milestone changes or migration implementation; scoped implementation decisions are recorded in the CPU plan.

state.reason: CPU model and explicit feature policies belong to the VM and never depend on Controller-only policy. Discovery cache is transient.
state.record: Existing Core managed journal command VM specifications and pool master pool-vms Spec records persist VMCPU.features with its named model. A fresh Controller recovers the unchanged definitions from host managed inventory.
state.recovery: A fresh Controller adopts the existing managed VM definitions through host inventory; no CPU recomputation changes saved definitions.

verification.method: Focused Go CPU checks, real mTLS peer tests with substituted CPU commands, UI unit/typecheck/build and full simulated browser walkthrough passed. Native Debian13 libvirt11.3/QEMU10 accepted fixed baselines and refused an unsupported instruction. API contract and privacy checks passed. The full Go race suite passed; documentation, generated reference freshness and diff checks passed. Scope and remaining hardware/migration limits are recorded in QA.
